author: Mark Atwood
text: DECISION 2026-05-12 (Mark, interactive): A) Shared public bridge crate. Two new workspace crates pkix-zlint-bridge and pkix-pkilint-bridge are filed as architectural commitments (PKIX-jy95.7 and PKIX-jy95.8). The adapter crates pkix-policy-zlint and pkix-policy-pkilint become thin wrappers over the bridge crates that expose findings as Lint-trait impls. pkix-difftest's zlint/pkilint differential oracles (PKIX-hbzo.1) consume the same bridge crates. Architectural rationale: (1) prelaunch 'done right from the start' framing favors architectural completeness over minimum-viable; two distinct consumers of identical functionality is exactly the case where shared infrastructure earns its keep. (2) Workspace precedent is pkix-revocation-http -- it IS the shared HTTP-fetching infrastructure that's also the runtime adapter for online revocation. pkix-*-bridge follows the same pattern. (3) AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 cache-friendliness flows through naturally: bridge types derive Clone+Send+Sync+serde feature-gate from day one; consumers inherit automatically. CASCADES: PKIX-jy95.1 (lint granularity), .2 (severity mapping), .3 (batch interface shape), .4 (error-handling policy) are now decisions about the BRIDGE crate API, not the adapter API. The bridge owns the subprocess plumbing; adapters expose findings via Lint trait. Open downstream questions: bridge sync vs async (default sync; async via separate trait or function), bridge version-pinning for upstream tools (zlint, pkilint), bridge API surface (single 'run on cert' vs batch + streaming). These are implementation-time decisions for PKIX-jy95.7 and .8.
